Question: If \(q_1(x)\) and \(r_1\) are the quotient and remainder, respectively, when the polynomial \(x^8\) is divided by \(x+\frac12,\) and if \(q_2(x)\) and \(r_2\) are the quotient and remainder, respectively, when \(q_1(x)\) is divided by \(x+\frac12,\) then \(r_2\) equals
Solution:
Method 1: Evaluate the first quotient

Let \(a=-1/2\), so the divisor is \(x-a\). Polynomial division gives
\[
x^8=(x-a)q_1(x)+r_1.
\]
Substituting \(x=a\) yields \(r_1=a^8\). We can therefore find the quotient by factoring \(x^8-a^8\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
q_1(x)&=x^7+ax^6+a^2x^5+a^3x^4\\
&\quad+a^4x^3+a^5x^2+a^6x+a^7.
\end{aligned}
\]
To verify this expression, multiply it by \(x-a\). All the middle terms cancel, leaving \(x^8-a^8\).

For the second division, substituting \(x=a\) into \(q_1(x)=(x-a)q_2(x)+r_2\) gives \(r_2=q_1(a)\). Each of the eight terms in the displayed quotient becomes \(a^7\), so
\[
r_2=8a^7
=8\left(-\frac12\right)^7
=\boxed{-\frac1{16}},
\]
choice B.

Method 2: Read the coefficient after shifting

Combining the two division identities places both remainders in one equation:
\[
x^8=\left(x+\frac12\right)^2q_2(x)
+r_2\left(x+\frac12\right)+r_1.
\]
Set \(t=x+1/2\), so \(x=t-1/2\). Then
\[
\left(t-\frac12\right)^8
=t^2q_2\left(t-\frac12\right)+r_2t+r_1.
\]
On the right, the first term has no constant or linear term because it is a polynomial multiplied by \(t^2\). Thus \(r_2\) is precisely the coefficient of \(t\) on the left.

The left side is a product of eight factors \((t-1/2)\). A linear term is obtained by choosing \(t\) from exactly one factor and \(-1/2\) from each of the other seven. There are eight choices for that one factor, so the coefficient is
\[
r_2=8\left(-\frac12\right)^7
=\boxed{-\frac1{16}},
\]
choice B.
